sections.h2: What are the quick ways to sell a house in San Juan?
sections.html:
San Juan owners generally weigh three paths: an agent listing, a sale on their own, or a cash offer for the house in its current state. Cash is the shortest route, and a listing tends to bring the highest price for a house in good shape.

San Juan lies in south central Hidalgo County on Farm Road 1426 and State Highway Spur 374, about six miles northeast of McAllen, according to the Texas State Historical Association. Its school district name, Pharr-San Juan-Alamo, shows how closely the three towns are linked.

Before you accept any offer, ask what it assumes about repairs, who pays recording and title costs, and the closing date. A written answer to each lets you compare offers on equal terms.

sections.h2: What is San Juan's history, and how does it affect housing?
sections.html:
San Juan was organized in 1909 and reportedly named for John Closner. The city incorporated on December 29, 1917. The townsite lies on land from two Spanish grants made in 1767, and the Handbook says the first school building went up in 1918.

The economy grew from irrigated farming, with a cotton compress, a cannery and a cotton gin built in 1924. By 1945 the town had the largest plant in the South making concrete pipe for irrigation drainage, plus citrus and vegetable packing houses. The Virgen de San Juan del Valle Shrine, built in 1954, draws pilgrims and tourists, and a new shrine was dedicated in April 1980.

The Handbook records growth from 4,371 people in 1960 to 10,815 in 1992 and 26,229 in 2000. That fast growth means many houses are fairly recent, so keep receipts and records for repairs you have made.

sections.h2: Which school district and appraisal district cover a San Juan house?
sections.html:
The Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District, established on March 24, 1919, took in all of the schools in San Juan, according to the Handbook. Check your tax bill to confirm the district listed for your parcel.

Its website offers property search, an online portal for filing exemptions and appeals, and a homestead portal for homestead and over 65 applications. The district said it is accepting applications for Appraisal Review Board auxiliary members for 2026 and 2027, and its customer service line is 956-381-8466.

  • Use the property search to see your value, owner and tax history.
  • Use the portal to file an exemption or an appeal.
  • Use the truth in taxation site to see proposed rates from each taxing unit.
  • Use the Comptroller's taxpayer pamphlet for the protest process.

Ask the county tax office for your bill and the exact rate for each unit. We do not state a rate here because each unit sets its own.

sections.h2: What does the Virgen de San Juan del Valle Shrine mean for the city?
sections.html:
The shrine, built in 1954, drew pilgrims and tourists almost at once. The Handbook adds that on October 23, 1970 a rented single engine plane struck it while more than 130 people were inside, causing about $1.5 million in damage, and that a mass effort rebuilt it. The new shrine was dedicated in April 1980.

By the mid 1960s San Juan reported ten churches, three schools, two hospitals, a library, a bank and a newspaper, and the Handbook calls its economy agriculture and commerce with visitors to the shrine also important. The city is also known as home of the Bougainvillea Trail of Texas.

For a seller this means visitor traffic and a stable local identity, but no guarantee of price. Describe your block, its distance to schools and the shrine, and any recent work in plain terms.

sections.h2: What do the city's planning and permit offices handle in San Juan?
sections.html:
The City of San Juan Planning Department manages land use, zoning, permits, subdivisions and rezoning. It is made up of Health, Building and Code Enforcement divisions that watch zoning, safety and health rules. The office is at 512 S. Nebraska Ave. and can be reached at 956-223-2220.

The city runs an interactive GIS map that shows zoning and city limits, and it helps you find out whether you need city permits or utilities. It also lets you check whether a location falls under Hidalgo County Precinct 1 or 2 for services outside city jurisdiction.

Owners near the edge of town should start there. Whether a parcel sits inside city limits changes who regulates a garage conversion, an addition or a fence. Ask the office whether a permit is on file for earlier work.

sections.h2: How do Texas tax penalties work if you owe on a San Juan house?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in the fall, and the Comptroller says unpaid taxes are delinquent from February 1.

The table below lays out how the penalty builds up after that, as printed by the Comptroller.

Delinquent tax penalties in Texas (Texas Comptroller)
WhenPenalty or interest
February 1Six percent penalty and one percent interest
Each month until July 1Penalty continues to rise one percent a month; interest is one percent a month
July 1Penalty becomes 12 percent
After attorney referralUp to 20 percent more if the unit has an attorney contract

A written request to waive penalty and interest has to be filed before the 181st day after the delinquency date. Installment plans of up to 36 months exist at some collectors and are required only for a residence homestead.

sections.h2: How do deeds, probate and tenants work for a San Juan seller?
sections.html:
Deeds for San Juan land go to the Hidalgo County Clerk, and the signer must appear before a notary or other authorized officer.

For an inherited house, a will can be probated within four years of the death, and a muniment of title can pass title when the estate has no debts apart from liens on the land. Heirs often need a title company to tell them which document a buyer's lender will accept.

A tenant complicates timing. Removal needs written notice and a justice court case, while selling with the tenant in place skips that process and keeps rent coming until closing.

sections.h2: What if the house is in foreclosure or needs major work?
sections.html:
Foreclosure in Texas is usually nonjudicial and ends in a public auction. A sale before that date can protect your equity, and excess proceeds after an auction go to junior liens before the former owner.

A house that needs a new roof, drainage work or electrical repairs suits an as is buyer, who takes on the work. You give up some price in exchange for skipping contractors and repair requests.

faqs.q: What school district is San Juan in?
faqs.a: The Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District, which the Handbook of Texas says was established in 1919 and took in all of the schools in San Juan. Your tax bill confirms it for your parcel.

faqs.q: Who appraises property in San Juan?
faqs.a: The Hidalgo County Appraisal District. It offers a property search, an online portal for exemptions and appeals, and a customer service line at 956-381-8466.

faqs.q: Does San Juan have a planning office I can call about permits?
faqs.a: Yes. The Planning and Zoning department handles permits, zoning and rezoning, and can be reached at 956-223-2220. Its GIS map helps you check city limits and zoning.

faqs.q: When do unpaid taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1 for most bills, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest start. The penalty rises to 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Can an unpaid tax bill stop a San Juan sale?
faqs.a: It does not have to. A tax lien attaches on January 1, so the unpaid amount is normally settled from your proceeds at closing. Ask the county tax office for a payoff figure and have your title company include it.
